root_idea.summary: The root centers on raising something upward, especially by building it up or making it high.
root_idea.development: This orientation extends from raising a structure with gypsum or mortar to making a building lofty or strongly constructed, and figuratively to raising the voice or publicizing something.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized masculine passive-participle citation form مَشِيدٌ.
Displayed under the normalized masculine Form II passive-participle citation form مُشَيَّدٌ rather than the inflected Quranic surface form مُشَيَّدَة.

senses.definition: Plastered with gypsum or similar mortar; built using such material.
senses.usage_conditions: Applied to a palace or other structure, including the Quranic expression قَصْرٍ مَشِيدٍ.

senses.definition: Built up high; lofty, of a palace or other structure.
senses.usage_conditions: The high or lofty interpretation is closely related to the elevation produced by the building or plastering described in the first sense.

senses.definition: Firmly or extensively built, including construction with gypsum or similar plaster.
senses.usage_conditions: Applied to a building or structure; the Quranic surface form is مُشَيَّدَةٌ.

senses.definition: Raised high; lofty or high-built, of a building.
senses.usage_conditions: The Form II passive can carry the implication of repeated or extensive building, by which a structure becomes high; the Quranic occurrence is the lexical plural form مُشَيَّدَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To plaster a wall with gypsum or similar material; to build a structure with it.
To strengthen and exalt something figuratively, as in strengthening or exalting a religion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A metaphorical usage, also associated with the meanings of شَيَّدَ and أَشَادَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Calling camels, including raising the voice while doing so.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An infinitival usage in the construction شَادَ بِالإِبِلِ.
An attributed infinitival usage of شَادَ; the lexicographic transmission records textual variation around its form.
Recorded as a verbal usage said of a man.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To build firmly or strongly and raise high, especially a palace or other building.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II may imply repeated or extensive building.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To raise the voice in proclaiming something, make it known, or publicize it; by extension, to raise a person's fame or publish a favorable or unfavorable report.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with constructions such as أَشَادَ بِهِ, أَشَادَ بِذِكْرِهِ, and أَشَادَ عَلَيْهِ.
A Persian-derived homograph identified as distinct from the native lexical development of شيد.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Gypsum or similar material used to plaster a wall; mortar or clay-like plaster.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Names the construction material rather than the completed building.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Calling camels and raising the voice.
Firmly building and raising a structure.
Proclaiming, publicizing, and raising fame or reports.
Quran-attested meanings of مَشِيدٌ and مُشَيَّدٌ: plastered or built with gypsum, and high or lofty construction.

cautions: The modern Quran locations shown here are the QAC-supplied locations; historical citation notation in the lexical discussion has not been converted into modern verse numbering.
The interpretations 'built or plastered with gypsum' and 'lofty' are closely connected in the evidence, with loftiness presented as the result or characterization of elevated construction.
شَيْدٌ meaning possessed, insane, or intoxicated is explicitly identified as Persian-derived and is retained as a homographic lexical item rather than assumed to be a native root derivative.
